_purpose: Single hand-authored home for VIEW prose (Charter R4): the claim-kind + search-facet display-label maps, the claim-kind -> colour-category map (the LOCKED colour language, redesign blueprint §6), plus generic UI chrome copy for the entity-page redesign. ID-referenced, single-copy, never inline in views/. Authored like glossary.json / doctrine-data.json, NOT a pillar projection (view copy has no Wallach source, carries no dose/number). kind_labels + kind_categories cover every distinct claim.kind in the sealed corpus (gated by kind_label_covers_corpus + claim_category_mapping_total). facet_labels is the single home for the search-facet headers (the former core FACET_LABEL literal moved here). ui holds generic chrome copy and GROWS as each view is migrated (H2-H4).
_note: Values match the pre-redesign display exactly so H0 makes no visual change: kind_labels == the old corpusKindLabel slug->UPPER transform; facet_labels == the former core/schemas/search.ts FACET_LABEL byte-for-byte. kind_categories added in H1 (derivation-correctness): the semantic colour FAMILY per kind per the locked colour language -- green = what-to-do (protocol/dose), teal = the-science (mechanism/definition/diagnostics/interaction/food-source), amber = signs (deficiency/toxicity), orange = Wallach's-positions (prevalence/prognosis/quote), violet = story/lore (personal-anecdote), red = cautions (contraindication). §6 fixes 11 of the 14 kinds explicitly; quote->orange, personal_anecdote->violet, food_source->teal are H1 defaults pending Luneth review. The concrete CSS --sr-facet-accent value for each family lives in the stylesheet (H2/H6), never here (colour value = presentation, family key = semantics).

ui.kd_ep_fam_bracket: you must eat these — the 2 in the 90
ui.kd_ep_o3_kill: One from plants. Two from the sea.
ui.kd_ep_fam_kill: Three fatty acids. You only have to eat two.
ui.kd_ep_fam_note: Note: 'omega-9' (oleic acid) is a different fat — not one of these three. It sits on this table for the familiar '3-6-9' trio, not because Wallach counts it.
ui.kd_ep_fam_s1_b: Linoleic (an omega-6) and linolenic (an omega-3). Your body can't make either one, so they have to come from food — these are the two fatty acids counted in the 90.
ui.kd_ep_fam_s2_b: Arachidonic — a second form of omega-6. Wallach names it too, but your body builds it from linoleic, so it only turns essential-to-eat when you run low on the first. That is what 'conditionally essential' means.
ui.kd_ep_fam_s3_b: Both — and it is not a contradiction. He designates two as always-essential (the ones in the 90) and names three because arachidonic still has fatty-acid activity when you need it. Two you must eat; the third your body usually makes for you.
ui.kd_ep_mirror_body: Wallach's requirement is for the cobalt COMPLEX — vitamin B12 — not for cobalt itself. His own supplement table lists B12 at 400 mcg and no cobalt at all. So your cobalt rides on your B12, and cobalt listed on a label counts for nothing here.
ui.kd_ep_mirror_foot: He does call cobalt a cofactor for the thyroid hormone thyroxin — but puts no number on it.
ui.kd_ep_noness_body: Wallach's essential fatty acids are omega-3 and omega-6. Omega-9 (oleic acid) is not one of them — your body makes its own, and he never counts it toward the 90. We keep its tile because 'omega 3-6-9' is how these oils are named and sold — the Youngevity EFA blends included — so the three shown here match what you read on the bottle.
ui.kd_ep_noness_body2: What omega-9 is NOT: Wallach's own third fatty acid. That one is arachidonic — a second form of omega-6 that turns essential only when you run low on the first. A different molecule, and a different story.
ui.kd_ep_pdm_calc_tip: Wallach doses plant-derived colloidal minerals at {dose} per {perbw} of body weight, daily. One fl oz carries about {refmg} of mineral solids; for a {bw} reference adult that works out to {goal}.
ui.kd_ep_pdm_note: Wallach's thesis is that plant-derived colloidal minerals deliver the whole spectrum together — 60 to 72 minerals in one complex — so they share a daily target as one group, rather than one mineral at a time.
ui.kd_ep_present_body_structural: You get all you need from the air you breathe, the water you drink, and ordinary food. There is nothing to supplement, so no daily target is set.
ui.kd_ep_present_body_zero: Wallach's own supplement table lists this at a need of zero — you already get enough from food, so there is nothing to add.

ui.kd_foods_contrast_hd: What to change in your diet
ui.kd_foods_deck: Getting all 90 essential nutrients is only half of Dr. Wallach’s model. The other half — just as important — is removing the foods that keep your gut from absorbing them.
ui.kd_foods_form_hd: Sometimes it’s the form, not the food
ui.kd_foods_hl1: You are not what you eat.
ui.kd_foods_stat_body: Americans are gluten-intolerant — about one in three.
ui.kd_foods_villi_bad_cap: Flattened, blunted villi — nutrients slide past, unabsorbed.
ui.kd_foods_villi_explain: In plain terms: gluten inflames and wears down the gut’s absorbing surface — the tiny finger-like villi below. Stubby ones can’t catch the passing nutrients; tall, dense ones reach up and pull them into your blood.
ui.kd_foods_villi_gloss: The millions of tiny finger-like projections lining the small intestine. Their vast surface area is where nutrients are absorbed into the blood — flatten them (as gluten can) and absorption collapses.
ui.kd_foods_villi_note: This is the second prong in one picture: gluten gradually wears down the villi that do the absorbing, so even a flawless 90-nutrient regimen underperforms until the gut heals.
ui.kd_foods_villi_ok_cap: Tall, dense villi — a vast surface area that pulls nutrients in.

ui.kd_ep_pdm_hero_kill: Rock your body can't absorb — until a plant rebuilds it.
ui.kd_ep_pdm_s1_b: Ageless glaciers grind the parent rock of the great mountain ranges into a dust as fine as clay — “rock flour.”
ui.kd_ep_pdm_s2_b: That cloudy, mineral-rich water is “Glacial Milk” — what the long-lived cultures flood across their terraced fields.
ui.kd_ep_pdm_s3_t: The plant does what your gut can't.
ui.kd_ep_pdm_s3_b: Crops take up those hard rock minerals and rebuild them into an organic, water-soluble form.
ui.kd_ep_pdm_s4_t: Now your body can absorb it.
ui.kd_ep_pdm_s4_b: As plant-derived colloidal minerals, about 98% gets in — versus 8–12% for the same minerals as ground-up rock.
